preconditions.description: The number of vertices in the tree is between 6 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct vertices labeled from 1 to n.
The input contains exactly n-1 edges, forming a tree.
The edges form a connected undirected graph (a tree).

postconditions.expression: len(output_lines) == 2 and all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in output_lines)
postconditions.description: The output consists of exactly two lines, each containing two distinct vertex labels.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n and x != y for line in output_lines for x, y in [line.split()])
postconditions.description: Each vertex in the output pairs is labeled from 1 to n and distinct within a pair.

postconditions.expression: all(x1 != x2 and x1 != y2 and y1 != x2 and y1 != y2 for (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in zip(output_pairs, output_pairs[1:]))
postconditions.description: All four vertices in the two output pairs are distinct.

postconditions.expression: not any(v in path(x1, y1, edges) for v in [x2, y2]) and not any(v in path(x2, y2, edges) for v in [x1, y1])
postconditions.description: Neither vertex of one pair lies on the simple path between the vertices of the other pair.

postconditions.expression: len(set(path(x1, y1, edges)) & set(path(x2, y2, edges))) >= 2
postconditions.description: The two paths share at least two common vertices.

postconditions.expression: not exists((x1p, y1p), (x2p, y2p)) such that (len(set(path(x1p, y1p, edges)) & set(path(x2p, y2p, edges))) > len(set(path(x1, y1, edges)) & set(path(x2, y2, edges)))) or (len(set(path(x1p, y1p, edges)) & set(path(x2p, y2p, edges))) == len(set(path(x1, y1, edges)) & set(path(x2, y2, edges))) and (len(path(x1p, y1p, edges)) + len(path(x2p, y2p, edges))) > (len(path(x1, y1, edges)) + len(path(x2, y2, edges))))
postconditions.description: The output pairs maximize the number of common vertices between the paths, and among those, maximize the total path length.
